section.sectionSummaryBrief: The matter depends solely on our actions and service, for performing a mitzvah properly brings about a personal redemption for the one who fulfills it.
section.t: And the matter depends only on our actions and our service,
for through performing a mitzvah as it ought to be,
redemption is brought about,
the personal redemption of the one who fulfills the mitzvah,
that he finds himself in a state of true freedom,
as understood from what is explained in Iggeret HaKodesh
in the interpretation of the verse,
"He redeemed my soul in peace."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The personal redemption achieved through a mitzvah is eternal above and continues to affect the person below throughout his daily life, leading to the general redemption.
section.t: And one may add,
that the personal redemption
("He redeemed my soul in peace")
that is brought about through the fulfillment of a mitzvah as it ought to be, is not only at the time of fulfilling the mitzvah, but it continues also afterward.
And analogous to what is explained in Tanya
regarding the unification that is brought about through the fulfillment of a mitzvah,
that this unification above is eternal forever and ever,
and this
(the unification above)
also affects the person below,
so too is it regarding the matter of "He redeemed my soul in peace" that is brought about through the fulfillment of a mitzvah,
that it is an eternal matter above and also below
[and analogous to the saying of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,
"Whoever engages in Torah brings peace to the heavenly retinue and to the earthly retinue"],
that the personal redemption through the fulfillment of the mitzvah continues and acts throughout all the days of his life,
in his daily life.
And from this one also comes to the general redemption,
"And the kingship shall be Hashem's"
in all of existence entirely,
both above and below.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: There is a special virtue in matters explicitly connected to Moshiach, such as eating the Meal of Moshiach and drinking four cups on the last day of Pesach, which can immediately bring the future redemption.
section.t: And behold, in addition to this that all the matters of Torah and mitzvot
(our actions and our service)
bring near and bring about the future redemption,
there is a special virtue in those matters that are more explicitly connected to Moshiach.
And among them,
eating the Meal of Moshiach on the last day of Pesach and drinking the four cups at this meal.
For just as the four cups on the first nights of Pesach correspond to the four expressions of redemption
(the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt),
so too is it regarding the four cups of the Meal of Moshiach on the last day of Pesach, which are connected to the future redemption.
And one may explain this based on the explanations of the connection of the future redemption to the four cups,
to the four expressions of the redemption of the future,
and the future redemption will be from the four corners of the earth.
And perhaps one may add,

that this—that in the Meal of Moshiach there is the same number of cups as on the first nights of Pesach—is a hint that it is within the power of every single Jew to come immediately from the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt
(the four cups of the first nights of Pesach)
to the future redemption
(the four cups of the last day of Pesach),
a redemption in its simple sense
below ten handbreadths.
And especially since our actions and our service now are like a dwarf atop a giant,
because they come after and in continuation of the actions and service of our Rabbis, our leaders,
the Alter Rebbe, the Mitteler Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, the Rebbe Maharash, the Rebbe Rashab, and my master, father-in-law, the Rebbe,
surely and surely it is within the power of our actions and our service,
including eating the Meal of Moshiach and drinking the four cups on the last day of Pesach,
to bring the redemption immediately,
in the blink of an eye, literally.
